item.title: How AI demand puts upward pressure on DDR5 prices
item.description: Follow two routes from AI infrastructure orders to PC memory costs, then see where the evidence stops.

item.title: There isn't one AI bubble. There are six different businesses.
item.description: Follow the invoices from DRAM fabs to paying AI users to see who earns revenue and who carries the risk.

item.title: The GPU break-even equation nobody shows you
item.description: A per-GPU model for the price and billable hours needed to recover hardware, power, operations and the cost of capital.

item.title: The AI buildout is a critical-path problem
item.description: A deployment model shows why getting GPUs four months early can buy zero months of revenue and how to find the milestone that matters.

item.title: Five predictions that could falsify my AI boom thesis
item.description: Five public indicators with deadlines, baseline values and rules for scoring a miss.

item.title: What a sold-out HBM order book tells you
item.description: Follow a memory contract through deposits, shipment, deployment, and the economics of the application it ultimately serves.

item.title: What the AI buildout changes for a PC builder
item.description: A matched DDR5 kit shows why posted price and stock both matter, especially for a local AI workstation.

item.title: Why GPU rental and RAM prices can move in opposite directions
item.description: An AWS rate cut and a rising PC DRAM contract market show how installed capacity and fresh manufacturing respond to different constraints.

item.title: Where will the next AI infrastructure bottleneck move?
item.description: Track how scarcity can move from accelerator supply to power, networking, and customer demand using the throughput of one workload.

item.title: What happens when a GPU cluster hits a power limit?
item.description: Under the same site power cap, eight fast rack groups and twelve slower ones produce different queues. The better policy depends on the workload.

item.title: Will GPUs become obsolete before they pay for themselves?
item.description: A reproducible three- versus five-year cash-flow model shows why a working GPU can fall short of earning back its purchase price.

item.title: AI capex is climbing. What is happening to cash flow?
item.description: A filing-based comparison of Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta measures how much cash remained after equipment spending in the September quarters of 2025 and 2026.

item.title: The circular money flows behind AI infrastructure
item.description: Anthropic's AMD disclosure and CoreWeave's NVIDIA agreements show how hardware supply, equity and capacity commitments can point in opposite directions.

item.title: The true cost of serving one million AI tokens
item.description: Three public DeepSeek-R1 benchmark runs on the same rack show why a token cost estimate needs a latency target and an occupancy assumption.

item.title: AI demand, GPU utilization and profit are three different metrics
item.description: CoreWeave's Q3 2026 filing and a four-stage operating funnel show what each number can actually tell you.

item.title: The strongest evidence against the AI bubble narrative
item.description: Paid usage, measured business adoption and infrastructure consumption make the bullish case, with different limits.

item.title: You Cannot Grade an Agent You Only Read
item.description: Final messages alone cannot show how an agent’s interface behaved. Driving the real OpenCode TUI in a pseudo-terminal shows you the transcript, the pixels, and the tool calls behind it.

item.title: The Model Is Not the Agent — Inside DeepSeek Harness
item.description: A source-code deep dive into the execution loop, tool calling, context management, and state that turn an LLM into a working agent.

item.title: An engineering-first approach to technical thought leadership
item.description: A practical playbook for turning original engineering work into credible writing, reusable artifacts, and professional opportunities, with human review before publication.

item.title: Yes, Autonomous Kaggle-Solving Agents Already Exist
item.description: Autonomous Kaggle-solving agents are already built by Microsoft, Google and open source. Where the remaining opportunity lies: reproducibility, cost-aware experimentation and evaluation.

item.title: Your Personal AI Operating System
item.description: A minimal personal AI stack for an Indian household: one control plane, ten workflows, seven life domains, five scheduled jobs, and explicit permission boundaries.

item.title: The Browser Is the New Operating System
item.description: The browser now brokers identity, data, devices, and isolation. Treating it as a harmless window above the operating system leaves the real security boundary unseen.

item.title: Self-Improving AI Agents: A Recursive Taxonomy
item.description: Six families of self-improving AI agent, 109 methods, ranked: what each one changes about itself, how durable that change is, and the handful that matter.

item.title: The Staff+ Operating Model: a practical field guide to technical leadership
item.description: A field guide for Senior SWE to Tech Lead to Staff/Principal: leadership without authority, the four archetypes, four work pillars, and career traps.

item.title: Building Luffy: a PR review agent you can audit
item.description: A comment-triggered PR review control plane: Hermes Agent, OpenRouter, Claude Opus 5, and a hub memory that grows—built on a real Odoo bug.

item.title: Memori: The Recursive Design of Agent Memory
item.description: Agent memory is a retrieval problem, not a storage one. Why memory is really three problems—and why Memori stores rules about how to use itself.

item.title: Building Persistent Memory for AI Agents: Architecture Decisions in Memori
item.description: The engineering behind Memori, a persistent memory system for AI coding agents: hybrid RRF search, access-decay scoring, and cosine deduplication.

item.title: Hard Constraints Belong in Code: The Probabilistic-Deterministic Hybrid Agent Pattern
item.description: LLMs explore solution spaces; deterministic code guarantees correctness. High-stakes architecture wires both: model priors to explore, code to enforce.

item.title: Designing CLI Tools for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Memori
item.description: Designing command-line tools AI coding agents can actually use: output modes, error design, behavioral snippets, and making machines help themselves.

item.title: The AI-Augmented Developer Playbook: Architect, Delegate, Validate
item.description: Shifting from code-producing craftsman to AI-orchestrating architect: abstract thinking, pattern libraries, and rigorous validation for higher leverage.

item.title: Forging AI’s Lasting Memory: Lessons from Asimov and First Principles
item.description: Why modern AI agents forget, how Asimov's positronic robots managed memory, and a first-principles guide to memory that endures across sessions.

item.title: My Reading List for the next 10 years and Why
item.description: A decade-long, first-principles roadmap through epistemology, cognition, memory, and AI—the foundational texts shaping my path as a systems thinker.

item.title: Who Am I?
item.description: My cognitive operating system: first-principles thinking, recursive refinement, and systems thinking—and how I keep evolving as a systems engineer.
